thread:
client-dev: hey team — running into a weird streaming issue. Our client opens an SSE to /v1/streams with an auth token and gets data for ~2s then the connection is closed with a 429. The response body has partial content (last chunk incomplete). No obvious retries from the client.
client-dev: basic repro: we use EventSource in the browser -> receives a few events then an HTTP 429 arrives mid-stream. Headers we see: `x-request-id: req_01HabcXYZ`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 13`.
client-dev: example fetch header we send: `Authorization: Bearer sk-user-XXXX`. We suspect either quota or auth/account mismatch — the account dashboard shows quota left.
Sam (Support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the full root request id and a copy of the failing response (headers + body)? Also, did you rotate tokens recently or use any service account?
client-dev: pasted request-id above. Here's the failing response captured by our client: 
```\nHTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\nX-Request-Id: req_01HabcXYZ\nX-RateLimit-Limit: 100000\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\nX-RateLimit-Reset: 13\n\ndata: {"type":"partial","content":"...token stream fragment..."}\n\n```
client-dev: server log (tail) around the time: 
```
[2026-03-11T14:02:11Z] req=req_01HabcXYZ client=10.0.0.7 stream_open
[2026-03-11T14:02:13Z] req=req_01HabcXYZ client=10.0.0.7 tokens_emitted=420
[2026-03-11T14:02:13Z] req=req_01HabcXYZ -> 429 quota_exceeded tokens_accounted=880
```
client-dev: note tokens_emitted != tokens_accounted above — looks like double-count or a mismatch mid-stream.
Sam (Support): good catch on the mismatch. @Eden (Billing) can you check the token accounting for that org key at the timestamp? Might be a billing-side double-count bug recently reported.
Eden (Billing): looking now. I can see an anomaly — around 14:02 we had a spike where a background job (rate-queue-flusher v2.1) accidentally replayed a token accounting event for long-lived SSE connections. That caused a double-deduct in a 3-minute window for some streams. I pulled the ledger entry: `deduct org=org_12 amount=460 trace=replay_0a`.
Jess (SRE): tagging this as potentially both a billing and runtime issue. From the runtime side, our streaming path emits per-chunk token events and also flushes a deferred accounting event at close. If the flusher job retried on perceived failure, we could double-count. Need to confirm whether the SSE connection closed early and triggered the deferred flush while per-chunk counts were already committed.
Kai (Eng): repro plan: we should simulate a long SSE stream and induce a flusher retry. Steps: 
1) Start a stream with test key `sk-test-zz` and capture tokens emitted per-chunk.
2) Force the flusher to fail once (tcp reset) and then retry.
3) Observe accounting logs and X-RateLimit headers.

Kai (Eng): quick local repro script (node) to stress stream and emulate flusher failure: 
```\nconst EventSource = require('eventsource');\nconst es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-1');\nes.onmessage = e => console.log('evt', e.data);\nsetTimeout(() => { // trigger flusher retry via admin endpoint\n  require('node-fetch')('https://internal.admin/trigger-flusher-retry', {method:'POST'}).then(()=>console.log('triggered'));\n}, 1500);\n```
Sam (Support): while you run that, customer-side workaround suggestions? We can advise exponential backoff + reconnect and to check `Last-Event-ID` to resume. But we need to avoid losing tokens or double billing on resume.
client-dev: a resume token mechanism would help. Right now our client can't tell if the stream terminated because of quota or server glitch — we just see `429`.
Jess (SRE): status update: I deployed a canary to the flusher job to make it idempotent (guard against replays) — DeployBot: `canary deploy start rate-queue-flusher v2.1.1`
DeployBot: canary deploy initiated by @Jess (SRE) — 3 hosts (canary) — tracking logs at /deploys/2026-03-11/flusher-v2.1.1
ops-oncall: can confirm canary logs show no duplicate ledger writes for streams started after 14:10Z. Monitoring for 30m.
Eden (Billing): I've also placed a temporary credit offset for org_12 to undo the duplicate deduction at 14:02. Ledger rollback id `rollback_20260311_01` applied. Client should see quota restored immediately.
client-dev: tested now after the canary — client reconnected and got full stream without 429. We do see the server send `x-rate-limit-remaining` correctly. Thanks.
Sam (Support): recommend long-term fixes: 
- make flusher idempotent (done in canary),
- change streaming accounting to periodically checkpoint to avoid large deferred flushes,
- add streaming resume token in API so clients can safely reconnect without losing progress.

Kai (Eng): opened PRs: `runtime: idempotent-flusher` and `api: stream-resume-proto` with docs and client examples. PR urls: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/392 and https://git.internal/r/redwood/api/pulls/117
Sam (Support): customer follow-up message drafted: "We identified an edge case where a background flusher could replay accounting events for long-lived SSE sessions, causing premature quota exhaustion and 429 mid-stream. We've rolled out an idempotency fix and credited affected accounts. To avoid disruption, implement client-side reconnect with Last-Event-ID and exponential backoff. We'll add a stream-resume token in the API shortly." Would someone from eng sign off on wording? @Kai @Jess
Kai (Eng): LGTM. Add a short note in changelog and client best-practices.
Jess (SRE): closing monitor — no new 429 mid-stream incidents for org_12 in last 2 hours.
client-dev: confirming on our side too — no repro now. We'll keep an eye on production. Thanks everyone :pray:
Sam (Support): great — I'll mark this resolved in the ticket and follow up when the stream-resume API is live. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
